Subject: ACME POC discovery follow-up

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and the things we'd like to validate in the POC so we can move forward: 

- Primary goal: reduce avg. LLM inference latency for query pipelines while keeping quality drift < 2% on our key intents.
- Secondary: cost per 1M tokens and stability under bursty traffic.
- Success metrics we care about: 95th percentile latency, top-1 intent accuracy on the 8 core intents, and % of sessions with degraded responses.

We have a short internal eval window (4 weeks) and two environments we can use: staging (can accept online shadow traffic) and offline test (batch evaluation). Curious on your recommendation for methodology and whether you think online shadowing is required for a meaningful readout.

Samir
Head of ML Platform
Acme Corp

Thanks Samir - great call. Quick post-call recap and proposed evaluation plan (high level):

Summary of goals
- Primary: Meet 95th pctl latency target of < 450ms for the user query distribution you shared.
- Quality: <= 2% top-1 intent degradation on the 8 core intents vs your baseline model.
- Reliability: no more than 1% session failures under bursts simulated at 3x expected peak.

Proposed POC scope (4 weeks)
1) Week 0 (onboarding): access, example prompts + baseline snapshots, and confirm traffic shapes.
2) Week 1-2 (offline evals): run batched offline evals on the shared eval set; measure latency on representative sequence lengths.
3) Week 2-3 (online shadow): optional - mirror 10-20% of staging traffic to Redwood's shadow endpoint to capture real distribution. Provides strongest signal for regressions.
4) Week 3-4 (validation & handoff): run regression checks, review rubric, and finalize recommendations.

Owner matrix
- Redwood: Marissa (program lead), Vivek (SE lead for shadow/instrumentation)
- ACME: Samir (stakeholder), Leah (SRE contact for staging access)

Success criteria (attached: acme-poc-success-criteria.xlsx)
- Quantitative pass/fail thresholds for latency, intent accuracy, and failure rates.
- Grading rubric included for offline vs shadow evaluations (see eval-methodology-v1.docx).

Next steps
- Samir: confirm whether ACME can enable shadow in staging (approx 1 hour of config + allowlist IPs).
- Leah / SRE: share staging access mechanics (service account or temp creds).
- Redwood: we'll send a detailed test-run schedule and a short runbook for engineers.

Notes: offline-only evals are faster to set up and give clear baseline comparisons; online shadowing is recommended if you need coverage for emergent inputs and session-level metrics.

Best,

Quick technical notes on methodology and rubrics (attached: eval-methodology-v1.docx):

- Offline evals: we'll run your labeled eval set through the candidate models and measure top-1 intent accuracy, per-intent confusion, and token-level log-prob distributions. Offline pass = all core intents within 2% of baseline and no single-intent drop > 5%.
- Online shadow: mirror requests to Redwood endpoint; responses are scored asynchronously against your production labeler. Pros: session-level context, emergent prompt patterns. Cons: requires staging traffic and SRE support; slightly longer time to gather statistically significant samples for the rarer intents.
- Grading rubric (summary):
  * Green: meets latency & accuracy thresholds
  * Amber: meets either latency or accuracy but not both (action: tuning/quantization change or model variant)
  * Red: fails both (action: rollback and deeper analysis)

Instrumentation checklist for shadowing
- allowlist Redwood IPs (we'll provide)
- 10-20% mirror rate suggested; maintain <1% extra load on staging
- trace headers + sample payloads for debugging

I can own the run scripts and the evaluation harness; Vivek will coordinate the integration with your SRE for mirroring.
—Dev

Thanks - good questions, answered inline and next steps below.

1) Shadowing IPs & retention
- Redwood will provide a short IP allowlist (two egress IPs) and a simple runbook; we do not persist full payloads by default - we persist request/response metadata and sampled payloads for 7 days (can be adjusted under contract). I've attached acme-staging-access-instructions.txt with the allowlist and sample nginx mirror config.

2) Eval CSV
- Attaching a sample CSV spec in eval-methodology-v1.docx (column names: id,input_text,expected_intent,metadata_json). We'll also accept NDJSON if that's easier.

3) Timeline tweak
- Agree to compress shadowing to Week 2 (1 week mirror at 10%-15% traffic). We'll prioritize ramping instrumentation so you get useful signals quickly.

Next steps & owners
